finding.claim: Unauthenticated tokens force a synchronous JWKS refetch on every kid miss or missing kid, with no negative cache or refresh rate limit (DoS amplification, low to medium severity).
finding.source: Token header kid (or absent kid) in get_signing_key_from_jwt, jwks_client.py:213-226
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP fetch of the JWKS endpoint via urllib urlopen, jwks_client.py:117-118, with a 30 s default timeout (jwks_client.py:26)

trace.note: header.get("kid") from unverified token passed to get_signing_key
refresh=True skips the JWK set cache
urlopen network request per invalid token
_validate_kid only checks the kid is a string
match_kid returns None for kid=None, so a kid-less token also triggers a refetch

finding.guards_checked: api_jws.py:446-448 type check on kid only; no negative caching; no minimum refresh interval; no rate limit. Behaviour is documented in the docstring at jwks_client.py:188-190 ('refreshed and retried once'), but nothing bounds how often this happens.

finding.claim: Claim validators call int() on exp, nbf and iat but catch only ValueError, so null, array, object or JSON Infinity values escape as TypeError or OverflowError instead of a PyJWTError (low severity, error-handling).
finding.source: JWT payload with exp, nbf or iat set to null, an array, an object, or 1e400 (JSON Infinity), reaching the claim validators
finding.sink: int(payload[...]) in _validate_exp / _validate_nbf / _validate_iat, which raises an unhandled non-PyJWTError exception to the caller

trace.note: _merge_options defaults verify_exp etc. to False when verify_signature is False, so the path is reached only if the caller explicitly enables a claim check with signature verification off, or with an issuer-signed token

finding.guards_checked: Only ValueError is caught around int() (api_jwt.py:476-483, 491-494, 505-510). The caller's verify_exp/verify_nbf/verify_iat options gate reachability, and _merge_options disables them by default when signature verification is off. Requires either explicit caller configuration or a token signed by the issuer, so attacker-reachable only in that narrow configuration.
